title: Grateful Dead Live at The Matrix on 1966-12-01
lineage: SBD > Rm >Reel > Dat > CD > wav>  shnv3 > wav > shn

ai_review.summary: Cleaned‑up soundboard capture of a high‑energy early‑1966 Matrix set, highlighted by Garcia’s soaring Cream Puff War solo and rare Pigpen blues gems.
ai_review.review: The recording is a cleaned‑up soundboard tape that, while not crystal clear, offers a balanced mix with enough fidelity to enjoy the band’s early blues‑heavy set. The performance bursts with high energy, featuring a stellar Garcia solo on “Cream Puff War,” powerful Pigpen organ and vocals on tracks like “Death Don't Have No Mercy,” and several rare treats such as “Betty & Dupree” and “Deep Elem Blues.” Although some reviewers note pitch‑correction needs and occasional noise, the show is generally praised for its excitement and historic value.

ai_rating.rationale: Average star rating ~3.8 across 30 reviews, with most comments praising the musical performance and only moderate technical complaints; weighting favors show quality, yielding a solid above‑average score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Cleaner than earlier versions but still exhibits hiss, occasional pitch errors needing correction, and some file corruption (Cream Puff War). Reviewers suggest EQ tweaks; overall mix is balanced with decent instrument separation.

standout_songs: See That My Grave Is Kept Clean
poor_songs: You Don't Love Me (not as hot as other versions)
show_quality.setlist_flow: A blues‑heavy early‑Dead set at the Matrix, packed with rare tunes and multiple repeats of “Me & My Uncle.” The pacing is energetic but occasionally repetitive; nevertheless the rarity of many tracks makes the flow compelling for collectors.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s solo on “Cream Puff War” described as stellar; his vocal delivery on “Death Don't Have No Mercy” praised.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s Vox organ and vocals highlighted as driving the blues feel; his performances are called a must‑have for fans.
